cp_01: The sixty-second pitch. This is the hallway at C E L A, the introduction after a panel, the thirty seconds you get before someone's attention moves on. You are not closing here — you are earning a real meeting. One clean minute, then a specific ask.
cp_02: The structure, four beats. Hook — name the pain in one line. What — say what one three seven is in a sentence. Proof — the one detail that makes it credible. Ask — a specific next step. Hook, what, proof, ask. Memorize the shape, not a paragraph.
cp_03: Here is the sixty-second version, close to word for word. You know the ninety-minute intake where someone rebuilds a worker's whole file by hand? one three seven flips that — the worker organizes their own employment record, every fact linked to its source, and chooses to send it to your firm already organized. You open a clean, verifiable file instead of a shoebox. Could I get you a firm code to try it on one real intake?
cp_04: The ask is the most important sentence, so make it concrete and small. Not — are you interested — that invites a no. Instead: could I set you up with a firm code to try it on one intake this month? A specific, low-cost yes. Then stop talking and let them answer.
cp_05: If they lean in, you have three minutes. Expand only where they showed interest. Add Coverage Rate — how much of what the law requires is already on file. Add the worker-owns-it point, which is why it is not a referral service. And add one honest line: we use A I to organize, but every fact is source-linked, so nothing is taken on faith.
cp_06: The do-nots, because a cold pitch is where people oversell. Do not claim it scores or picks cases. Do not promise outcomes. Do not name a price in a hallway — earn the meeting first. And do not run past sixty seconds; a tight pitch that ends in a question beats a long one that ends in a monologue.
cp_07: That is the whole tool — hook, what, proof, ask, then silence. If you only remember one thing, remember the ask: a firm code, one intake, this month. Small, specific, and clean. Now go start a conversation.
